title: John XXII’s Veronica prayer (with huge indulgences) is aimed at Christ’s face-image on the sudarium, asking it to purge and lead to the blessed
source_text: XXV. Reperitur & Oratio quaedam, quae fertur a Johanne Papa XXII. edita, cum concessione indulgentiarum decies mille dierum illam devote dicentibus, inspiciendo Veronicam, ad quam oratio illa dirigitur. Vocatur autem Veronica effigies quaedam vultus Christi impressa Sudario, quod in aede Sancti Petri Romae asservari dicitur, ut etiam in quadam civitate Hispaniae, teste Marineo Siculo libro quinto de rebus Hispanicis. Ista vero Imago Veronica dicitur nomine mulieris, a qua Sudarium traditur faciei Christi sanguine & sudore aspersae admotum esse, & vultus ejus effigiem in se retinuisse. Porro sic se habet oratio illa quae legitur in libro qui Antidotarius animae inscribitur. Salve Sancta facies Nostri Redemptoris, In qua nitet species divini splendoris, Impressa panniculo nivei candoris, Dataque Veronicae signum ob amoris. Salve decus saeculi, speculum Sanctorum, Quod videre cupiunt spiritus coelorum; Nos ab omni macula purga vitiorum, Atque nos consortio junge beatorum. Salve vultus Domini imago beata, Ex aeterno munere mire decorata: Lumen funde cordibus ex vi tibi data, Et a nostris sensibus tolle colligata. Salve robur fidei nostrae Christianae, Deliruens haereticos qui sunt mentis vanae: Horum auge meritum qui te credunt sane. Salve nostrum gaudium in hac vita dura, Labili & fragili, cito peritura: Nos deduc ad propria, O felix figura, Ad videndum faciem quae est Christi pura.
pass_a_gloss: There is also found a certain Prayer which is said to have been published by Pope John XXII, with a grant of indulgences of ten thousand days to those devoutly saying it while looking upon the Veronica, to which that prayer is directed. But Veronica is called a certain effigy of Christ’s face impressed on a Sudarium, which is said to be kept in the church of Saint Peter at Rome, as also in a certain city of Spain, by the testimony of Marineus Siculus in the fifth book on Spanish affairs. But that Image is called Veronica by the name of the woman by whom the Sudarium is handed down to have been applied to Christ’s face sprinkled with blood and sweat, and to have retained His face’s likeness in itself. And the prayer reads in the book titled Antidotarius animae: Hail, Holy face of Our Redeemer… Hail, image of the Lord’s countenance… Pour light into hearts by the power given to you… Lead us to see the face which is Christ’s pure face.
pass_b_english: John XXII’s indulged Veronica prayer is directed to the sudarium face-image itself—asking the ‘holy face’ / ‘blessed image’ to purge, enlighten, and bring the devout to Christ’s pure face.

lemmas.gloss: to which that prayer is directed

choices.why: Papal sponsorship of prayer aimed at an image.
rejected: prayer clearly only to Christ absent the image
